chunks: On the day when every man will find whatever of good he has earned and of evil, and is confronted with it, he shall wish that a distance appeared between him and that day -- (that it were far away). God bids you beware of Him, though compassionate is God to His votaries.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's good and evil deeds on the Day of Judgment according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the immediacy of divine accountability, where deeds are not merely recorded but vividly 'presented' (muḥḍaran), emphasizing the psychological weight of self-confrontation. The wish for a 'great distance' from evil underscores the regret of the unrighteous, contrasting with Allah's warning (yuḥadhirukum) which serves as a merciful prelude to His ultimate compassion (ra'ūf) for the servants.
